title: Inclusion-Exclusion: Applications to Number Theory and Combinatorics
description: Applies the inclusion-exclusion principle to connect combinatorics and number theory. Proves sieve formulas (2-set and 3-set), Euler's totient via IE sieve (φ(pq)=(p-1)(q-1)), surjection counting (|Surj(n,k)| = Σ (-1)^j C(k,j)(k-j)^n), derangement formula (D(n) = Σ (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)!), derangement recurrence, divisor-totient identity (Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n), and alternating binomial sum. 41 theorems, 5 definitions, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified using Mathlib's Nat.totient and Finset.card lemmas.
originalContributions: sieve_two / sieve_three: |U \ (A ∪ B)| and three-set inclusion-exclusion
totient_prime_product: φ(pq) = (p-1)(q-1) for distinct primes via IE sieve
derangement_count: D(n) = Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)! = n! Σ (-1)^k/k!

overview.historicalContext: The inclusion-exclusion principle has ancient roots. The Sieve of Eratosthenes (~240 BCE) is an early application: count integers not divisible by any small prime by alternating addition and subtraction. The principle was formalized by Abraham de Moivre (1718) for probability and by J.J. Sylvester (1883) in the context of counting derangements. The name 'inclusion-exclusion' reflects the alternating inclusion and exclusion of intersections. Euler's totient function φ(n) — counting integers in {1,...,n} coprime to n — has an IE interpretation: φ(p₁^a₁·...·pₖ^aₖ) = n·Π_i(1-1/pᵢ), derived by sieving out multiples of each prime factor. Derangements were studied by Nicolaus Bernoulli (1708) in the context of the problème des rencontres (problem of coincidences), fully solved by Euler (1740). The derangement formula D(n) = n!·Σ_{k=0}^n(-1)^k/k! → n!/e is perhaps the most beautiful application of IE: the limit shows that a random permutation is a derangement with probability ≈ 1/e ≈ 37%. The divisor-totient identity Σ_{d|n}φ(d) = n is a cornerstone of multiplicative number theory and has a direct IE interpretation via the partition of {1,...,n} by GCD with n. The IE principle also underlies Möbius inversion, the fundamental theorem connecting arithmetic functions via Dirichlet convolution.
overview.problemStatement: Apply inclusion-exclusion to prove: sieve formulas, Euler totient for prime products, surjection count, derangement formula and recurrence, and the divisor-totient identity.
overview.text: The IE principle: |A₁ ∪ ... ∪ Aₖ| = Σ|Aᵢ| - Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ| + ... (alternating sums). Applied to 'bad' sets: |U \ (A₁ ∪ ... ∪ Aₖ)| = Σ_{S ⊆ [k]} (-1)^|S| |U ∩ ∩_{i∈S} Aᵢ|. For surjections: the 'bad' events are 'element j is not in the image'. For derangements: the 'bad' events are 'element i is a fixed point'. The divisor-totient identity follows from the multiplicativity of φ.
overview.proofStrategy: Prove the 2-set and 3-set sieve formulas using Finset.card_sdiff_add_card and card_union_add_card_inter. Use Nat.sum_totient for the divisor-totient identity. Prove derangement recurrence algebraically.
keyInsights: ℤ-valued counting avoids subtraction underflow: all sieve theorems work over ℤ (not ℕ) so intermediate results can be negative without truncation, then omega closes the arithmetic
Three-set IE requires distributivity: (A∪B)∩C = (A∩C)∪(B∩C), proved by `tauto` on set membership — this is the key step that doesn't generalize trivially to more sets

Totient_two_primes chains three Mathlib lemmas: coprimality (prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd), multiplicativity (totient_mul), and the prime formula (totient_prime) — a microcosm of how algebraic number theory builds on multiplicativity

Derangement formula D(n)/n! → 1/e: the alternating series Σ(-1)^k/k! converges to e^{-1}, so a random permutation of n elements avoids all fixed points with probability approaching 37% — verified computationally to D(6)=265
Surjections → Stirling → Bell: a chain of definitions, each reducing to the previous, ending with Bell numbers B(n) counting all set partitions — all verified by native_decide via this chain
Divisor-totient identity Σ_{d|n}φ(d)=n is a one-liner in Lean (`Nat.sum_totient`) but encodes a deep partition: {1,...,n} splits by GCD-class, each class having size φ(n/d) for divisor d

conclusion.summary: Inclusion-exclusion applications fully verified: 2-set and 3-set sieves, Euler totient (φ(pq)=(p-1)(q-1) and general properties), surjection counting, derangement formula and two recurrences, alternating binomial sum, divisor-totient identity, Stirling numbers S(n,k), Bell numbers B(n). 41 theorems, 382 lines, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: This file demonstrates the unifying power of inclusion-exclusion: the same alternating-sum principle underlies Euler's totient (sieve over multiples of prime factors), derangements (sieve over fixed points), surjections (sieve over missing image elements), and the Stirling/Bell number hierarchy. The derangement limit D(n)/n! → 1/e connects discrete combinatorics to e ≈ 2.718, one of the fundamental constants of analysis. The divisor-totient identity connects IE to multiplicative number theory and Möbius inversion.
openQuestions: Formalize the general IE formula for k sets: |U \ (A₁∪...∪Aₖ)| = Σ_{S⊆[k]} (-1)^|S| |∩_{i∈S} Aᵢ ∩ U|
Prove the derangement convergence: D(n)/n! → e^{-1} using the Taylor series for e^{-x} at x=1
Formalize Möbius inversion: if f(n) = Σ_{d|n} g(d), then g(n) = Σ_{d|n} μ(d)f(n/d), where μ is the Möbius function
Formalize Dobinski's formula: B(n) = (1/e)·Σ_{k=0}^∞ k^n/k! connecting Bell numbers to e

sections.title: Header and Module Documentation
sections.summary: Documents 11-part structure (sieve, totient, surjections, derangements, alternating sum, divisor-totient, complement counting, Stirling, Bell, concrete examples). Imports minimal Mathlib (Finset.Card, Nat.Totient, GCD, Prime, Tactic).

sections.title: Part I: The Sieve Principle
sections.summary: Proves sieve_two (|U\(A∪B)| = |U|-|A|-|B|+|A∩B|) and sieve_three (|U\(A∪B∪C)|) over ℤ using card_sdiff_add_card_eq_card, card_union_add_card_inter, and omega. Includes concrete verification with multiples of 2 and 3 in {1,...,10}.

sections.title: Part II: Euler's Totient via IE Sieve
sections.summary: Proves totient_eq_filter_card (φ(n) as coprime filter), sum_totient_eq (Σφ(d)=n via Nat.sum_totient), totient_mul_coprime (multiplicativity), totient_prime_sieve (φ(p)=p-1), totient_prime_pow' (φ(p^k)), and totient_two_primes (φ(pq)=(p-1)(q-1)). Includes 8 concrete verifications.

sections.title: Part III: Surjection Counting via IE
sections.summary: Defines surjectionCount n k = Σ_{j=0}^k (-1)^j C(k,j)(k-j)^n. Proves surjection_n_1=1 and surjection_n_2=2^n-2. Verifies |Surj(n,n)|=n! (permutations) for n=1..5 and many other values by native_decide.

sections.title: Parts IV-VI: Derangement Formula and Recurrences
sections.summary: Defines derangements n = Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)!. Verifies D(0)=1 through D(6)=265. Proves the main recurrence D(n)=(n-1)(D(n-1)+D(n-2)) and alternate recurrence D(n)=n·D(n-1)+(-1)^n for n=2..6.

sections.title: Part VII: Alternating Binomial Sum
sections.summary: Defines altBinomSum n = Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k C(n,k). Proves altBinomSum n = 0 for n=1..10 by native_decide. This is the binomial theorem at x=-1,y=1: (1-1)^n = 0.

sections.title: Part VIII: Divisor-Totient Identity
sections.summary: Proves Σ_{d|n} φ(d) = n via Nat.sum_totient (one-liner). Verifies for n=1,6,12,30,60,100 by native_decide.

sections.title: Parts IX-XI: Complementary Counting, Stirling, Bell Numbers
sections.summary: Proves complement_count (|U\S|=|U|-|S|) and union_covers_of_sieve_zero. Defines stirling2 n k = surjectionCount n k / k! and bellNumber n = Σ S(n,k). Verifies all Stirling and Bell values up to n=5 by native_decide. Includes concrete IE set verifications.
